notable_absence.finding: The page states the character filter's actual mechanism precisely - 'In the Regular Expression field, enter the regular expression for the character filter' and '(Optional) In the Replacement field, enter a string that replaces any matches for the regular expression' - i.e. a regex match-and-replace, with replacement optional (implying deletion when omitted). I did not model this as a relation: the registry has no predicate shaped for 'the subject construct is configured by naming a regex pattern and an optional replacement string' - hasDefaultValue is the nearest fit but is for a setting's value-when-unset, not an optional sub-parameter, and forcing it would assert a default ('empty replacement = deletion') the page itself never states.

cross_component_finding: Same composition family as create-custom-analyzer.json in this batch: this page's own Next Steps line ('you can use it with a custom analyzer') independently corroborates the hasInternalComponent(search:custom-analyzer, search:character-filter) relation from a second page, with its own quotable evidence rather than a shared one - two separate pages in this batch each independently state the same containment fact in their own words ('before tokenizing' on the analyzer page; 'use it with a custom analyzer' here).
